app.tag: Pull the structure out of an argument and test its logic.
settings.title: Settings
lab.title: Logic Lab
lab.intro: Check whether a conclusion follows logically from the premises. Enter logical formulas below, not ordinary sentences or labels such as “premise 1:”. Select a step from your analysis to revise its formalisation and compare the result.
lab.review.title: Reconsider a step from your analysis
lab.review.intro: The original claims stay visible. Edit the formulas to see whether the conclusion still follows.
lab.review.step: Inference step from your current analysis
lab.review.noformal: This step has no formalisation yet. You can enter logical formulas below.
lab.conclusion: Conclusion (leave empty to test the premises only)
syntax.title: Notation
syntax.quant: for all x, there is an x
syntax.scope: a quantifier binds tightly; use a dot or parentheses for wider scope. There are no function symbols: use predicates.
v.valid.sub: Every valuation that makes all premises true also makes the conclusion true.
v.vacuous.sub: The premises can never all be true together, so anything follows. Look for the contradiction below.
v.invalid.prop: There is a valuation where all premises are true and the conclusion is false.
v.invalid.fol: Countermodel found with {n} element(s): all premises true, conclusion false. This proves invalidity.
v.valid_bounded.sub: Searched: all models with 1 to {n} elements. That is strong evidence but not a proof: validity in predicate logic is undecidable in general, and a countermodel may be larger or infinite.
v.vacuous_bounded.sub: No model with 1 to {n} elements makes all premises true. They may be truly contradictory, or only have infinite models (like the natural numbers with a successor relation).
v.unknown.sub: Lower the domain size or simplify the formulas.
v.satisfiable.sub: A valuation or model exists in which all formulas are true together.
v.unsatisfiable.sub: No valuation makes all formulas true at the same time.
v.unsat_bounded.sub: No model with 1 to {n} elements makes all formulas true.
sec.counter.hint: With these values all premises are true and the conclusion is false:
table.legend: Red: premises true, conclusion false. Green: premises and conclusion true.
core.text: These premises cannot all be true:
sec.repair: Hidden assumptions that would make the argument sound
repair.hint: Found by the engine: the premises plus this assumption make the conclusion valid, stay consistent, and do not already contain the conclusion itself.
import.note: In this countermodel {p} is empty. The argument silently assumes that at least one {p} exists (existential import).
err.title: I cannot read this
map.title: Argument map
map.intro: Paste a text or a passage from a paper. Agent 1 reconstructs the argument, agent 2 reads it critically, and the logic engine tests every step that can be formalised.
map.comingSoon: Start a two-agent argument analysis, inspect the map, and review disagreements.
map.text.ph: Paste an argument, essay or passage from a paper here…
map.trimmed: Only the first {n} characters are analysed.
map.nosample: The model capability is unavailable. Start the backend and choose Ollama or Anthropic in Settings.
map.empty: No analysis yet. Paste a text or pick an example and click Analyse.
map.inputRequired: Enter or choose a source text before starting the analysis.
map.noresult: The model returned no usable argument map. Please retry with a shorter text.
map.analysisFailed: Analysis failed. Check the selected model and try again.
d.select: Click a claim or an inference step (the round node) for details.

dis.title: Where do they disagree?
dis.intro: Per inference step side by side: what agent 1 thought, what agent 2 finds, and what the logic engine establishes. The strongest signal is a formalisation the engine refutes, or two formalisations with different outcomes: that usually marks a hidden assumption.
dis.comingSoon: Compare both agents' judgements and the logic engine's results.
logic.unavailable: The logic capability is not available.

model.intro: Choose Ollama for local analysis or Anthropic for API-based analysis. OpenAI support is coming soon.

f.engineA: The engine refutes agent 1's formalisation, which called the step strong.
f.engineB: The engine refutes agent 2's formalisation, which called the step strong.

f.vacuous: The premises of this formalisation are inconsistent.

ex.title: Export
rep.footer: Generated with Elenchos. The agents are language models and can make mistakes. The logic engine is exact for propositional logic; in predicate logic a found countermodel proves invalidity, but "no countermodel found" is not a proof of validity.
